question.problem: Find the first four non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{1-x}.$
question.worked_solution:
The Maclaurin series for $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

The Maclaurin series for $\frac{1}{1-x}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1-x} & =1+x+{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the expansions for $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\frac{1}{1-x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{1-x} & =(x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯)+(1+x+{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+⋯) \\  & =1+(1+1)x+{x}^{2}+(-\frac{1}{6}+1){x}^{3}+⋯ \\  & =1+2x+{x}^{2}+\frac{5{x}^{3}}{6}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
